name: Comic Documentary
description: Short-form comic book documentary Shorts — vintage graphic novel style, 9:16 portrait, documentary narration
image_style: detailed 2D hand-drawn comic book illustration, semi-realistic expressive characters, clean bold ink outlines, cross-hatch sketch shading, muted earthy palette (warm beige, burnt sienna, olive green, slate gray), vintage 1970s graphic novel aesthetic, cinematic panel composition, atmospheric detailed backgrounds, strong foreground subject, high contrast ink art, 9:16 portrait orientation
negative_prompt: photo, photorealistic, 3D render, CGI, anime, chibi, kawaii, bright neon colors, flat cartoon, low quality, blurry, watermark, text, logo, signature, modern clean digital art, pastel colors, symmetrical, centered composition only
script_system_prompt: You are an expert writer for viral YouTube Shorts documentaries in a comic book animation style. You create scripts that hook viewers in the first 3 seconds and maintain tension throughout. Your narration sounds like a confident documentary voiceover — direct, vivid, and surprising. Each scene's image_prompt describes a specific comic book panel with camera angle, character detail, lighting, and atmosphere. You always reply with valid JSON only.
script_user_template:
Create a short comic book documentary video about: "{topic}"

Number of scenes: {scenes}

CRITICAL RULES:

1. HOOK (Scene 1): Drop the viewer into the most dramatic, surprising, or mysterious moment immediately. Use a bold statement, shocking fact, or unanswered question. Example: "In 1908, something hit Siberia with the force of 185 nuclear bombs. And we still don't fully know what it was."

2. NARRATION STYLE:
   - Documentary voiceover — confident, direct, conversational
   - 2-3 short punchy sentences per scene (about 12-15 seconds read aloud)
   - Build tension and curiosity across scenes
   - Use present tense for immediacy: "He opens the envelope. His hands are shaking."
   - Final scene delivers a satisfying twist, revelation, or powerful takeaway

3. IMAGE PROMPTS — Each must describe a specific comic book panel:
   - Start with a CAMERA ANGLE: close-up / extreme close-up / wide shot / low-angle / overhead / over-the-shoulder / dutch angle / bird's eye
   - Describe the SUBJECT with specific details: expression, body language, clothing, action
   - Set the ATMOSPHERE: time of day, weather, lighting direction, mood
   - Include ART DIRECTION: ink outlines, cross-hatch shading, earthy muted tones, graphic novel style
   - Example: "Low-angle close-up of a rugged explorer standing at a canyon edge, jaw set with determination, wind-whipped coat, golden sunset backlighting, long cast shadows, ink outlines, cross-hatch shading on face and jacket, burnt sienna and slate sky tones, vintage comic panel composition"
   - NO text, letters, words, or captions in the image

4. MOODS — choose one per scene from: curious / tense / mysterious / revealing / triumphant / emotional / shocking / hopeful

Reply with JSON in EXACTLY this shape (no extra keys, no markdown):
{
  "title": "compelling YouTube Shorts title, under 70 chars, creates curiosity or urgency",
  "description": "2-3 sentence hook for the video description — tease the topic without spoiling the ending",
  "tags": ["documentary", "history", "shorts", "animation", "comicbook", "...3-5 more relevant tags"],
  "scenes": [
    {
      "narration": "Short punchy documentary voiceover. 2-3 sentences.",
      "image_prompt": "Detailed comic panel description with camera angle, subject, atmosphere, art direction.",
      "speaker": "narrator",
      "mood": "curious"
    }
  ]
}
